beside.label: Your notes, 19:06 UTC
beside.text: all that is ai paraphrasing me, but i'd qualify the "no use" part. I agree it is spiritual bypassing to claim the higher self is already perfect as a guide or parent. I have experienced myself the higher self perspective. What I can say about it is, it's a somewhat less subjective way of perceiving things as perfectly functioningin relaity despite the ego illusions. That matches what people say about it, but where I diverge from IFS is I don't think the higher self has any specific wisdom. It's a vanttage point where more wisdom and compassion can arise, but also a vantage point in which problems can seem like they were never problems at all, which could lead to LESS wisdom and compassion, and we see both of these operating in the guru types who supposedly embody their higher self, often within the same person. An excellent example is Anthony De Mello the jesuit syncretic perennial philosophy guy who emphasized overcoming egoic traps that lead away from present moment awareness, but who also was a psychotherapist and seemed to drift between different modes in a contradictory manner. so i think inner child therapy is more concretely drawing upon higher vantage points, the inner Guide being the analog of the Higher Self, which must coordinate and come after the Nurtuer and Protector roles without acting as a transcendent dismissive authority. obv that's not the prose for the guid exactly but maybe yopu can build from that. i think i am correctly characterizing IFS here but possibly oversimplifyhing since i know it's not exactly just one system and it has its own branches and disputes within it, which is another problem with it that i am trying to remedy by systematizing inner child therapy in the guide here... i should also point out that most inner child therapy does not sufficiently address the Guide (i think i did mention this) so it can go in the oppoosite extreme from IFS in that sense, so I'm trying to sort of bring together the best of both.

beside.text: all that is ai paraphrasing me, but i'd qualify the "no use" part. I agree it is spiritual bypassing to claim the higher self is already perfect as a guide or parent. I have experienced myself the higher self perspective. What I can say about it is, it's a somewhat less subjective way of perceiving things as perfectly functioningin relaity despite the ego illusions. That matches what people say about it, but where I diverge from IFS is I don't think the higher self has any specific wisdom. It's a vanttage point where more wisdom and compassion can arise, but also a vantage point in which problems can seem like they were never problems at all, which could lead to LESS wisdom and compassion, and we see both of these operating in the guru types who supposedly embody their higher self, often within the same person. An excellent example is Anthony De Mello the jesuit syncretic perennial philosophy guy who emphasized overcoming egoic traps that lead away from present moment awareness, but who also was a psychotherapist and seemed to drift between different modes in a contradictory manner. so i think inner child therapy is more concretely drawing upon higher vantage points, the inner Guide being the analog of the Higher Self, which must coordinate and come after the Nurtuer and Protector roles without acting as a transcendent dismissive authority. obv that's not the prose for the guid exactly but maybe yopu can build from that. i think i am correctly characterizing IFS here but possibly oversimplifyhing since i know it's not exactly just one system and it has its own branches and disputes within it, which is another problem with it that i am trying to remedy by systematizing inner child therapy in the guide here... i should also point out that most inner child therapy does not sufficiently address the Guide (i think i did mention this) so it can go in the oppoosite extreme from IFS in that sense, so I'm trying to sort of bring together the best of both.

beside.text: Insert in p3 as first sentence: "I don't know of a resource to find a perfect inner child therapist, and there are none which work with my guide yet, (although I can consult, and if you like the guide, you can ask a therapist to check it out and see what they agree with or disagree with as a great way to vet them). The best I could suggest at the moment is to search Open Path Collective (or a similar resource in your country), which lists thousands of affordable therapists. Filter for  Schema Therapy, since that's the one with the most similarity to my guide, but you'll find about 10x more Internal Family Systems therapists, which also overlap with reparenting in many ways. You can often find [even more Schema therapists at the official site](https://schematherapysociety.org/Search?&tab=1): 3x more on that page for NYC than via Open Path search when I checked."
